insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Basic Sum Insured: 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 & 50 Lakhs (Individual per insured person / Family Floater per policy, as per Schedule of Benefits)

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as multiplier benefit irrespective of any claims ... The maximum multiplier bonus will not exceed 100% of the Basic Sum Insured in any Policy Year.”
great.explanation: On renewal without a break, a 50% multiplier benefit is added irrespective of any claims, up to a maximum of 100% of the Basic Sum Insured. This means your cover can grow even if you claim, which is better than typical NCBs that reduce or reset after claims.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: No explicit statement found such as “no co-payment” or “X% co-payment applicable”, other than definition: “Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement...” and Reserve Benefit mentioning it can pay “Co-payment and / or Deductible for any health insurance claim”.
great.reference: Definition Def.6 Co-payment (page 4 approx.); Section B.4 Reserve Benefit (page 18 approx.)
great.explanation: No applied co-pay clause is stated; only a standard definition is present, and another benefit merely mentions co-pay/deductible as a type of expense. This indicates no co-pay is charged on the base plan, so admissible claims are not reduced by a mandatory percentage.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “a Restore Sum Insured (equal to 100% of the Basic Sum Insured) will be automatically available... The Restore Sum Insured can be used for only future claims... In case Family Floater Policy, Restore Sum Insured will be available for all Insured Persons in the Policy... IMPORTANT: In a Family Floater the Illness or disease will be covered in case a claim is made by any other Insured Person other than the Insured Person who has already claimed for that Illness or disease.”
good.explanation: An automatic restore of 100% of the Basic Sum Insured becomes available for future claims after the base sum insured is used. In a family floater, the same illness can be covered only if claimed by a different insured person than the one who already claimed for that illness.

good.name: Built-in SI Buffer
good.quote: “Any claims made under this benefit will not be subject to In-patient Benefit Sum Insured... This benefit covers... ii. Medical expenses incurred on inpatient and/or outpatient treatment. This includes - Co-payment and / or Deductible for any health insurance claim - Standard non-payable items under any health insurance claim ... - Additional inpatient medical expenses after exhaustion of sum insured.”
good.explanation: A separate “Reserve Benefit” can pay certain inpatient/outpatient expenses even after exhaustion of sum insured, and is stated to not be subject to the In-patient Benefit Sum Insured. This works like an extra insurer-funded buffer for items like deductibles/co-payments (if any) and standard non-payables.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day Waiting Period: Code-Excl03... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Treatment for illnesses is not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period and mainly affects claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.”
good.reference: Section C.1(ii) Specified disease/procedure waiting period (page 20 approx.)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. This is a common 2-year moratorium for certain conditions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are excluded for 36 months from the inception of the first policy. This 3-year PED waiting period is within normal market range.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I – List of Non-Medical Expenses” includes: “GLOVES”, “MASK”, “ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]”, “NEBULISATION KIT”, etc.
bad.reference: Annexure I – List of Non-Medical Expenses (pages 43-45 approx.)
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed in Annexure I (e.g., gloves, masks, kits) are not payable. This can increase out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization even when the main treatment is covered.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: No explicit room rent eligibility limit (e.g., “single private AC”, “any room”, “no capping”) found in provided text. Only definition: “Room Rent means the amount charged by a hospital for the occupancy of a bed...”
unclear.reference: Definition Def.40 Room Rent (page 8 approx.); Section B.1(a) mentions room rent as covered but no eligibility/cap provided (page 12 approx.)
unclear.explanation: Room rent is mentioned as covered, but the provided text does not state any room category eligibility or rupee cap. You may need to verify the Policy Schedule/benefit table to confirm whether any room rent limit applies (which can affect overall claim payouts).

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
